anchor: GitHub Actions artifact API server-stored archive sha256 digest and run/head/repository identity
scope: time-limited provider custody evidence, not owner signature nor permanent cryptographic transparency log

scenarios.expected: Actual native production PLAN_HANDOVER writes exactly two durable bundle files uploaded to Actions v4 artifact storage; independent job GETs artifact by numeric ID, checks provider run ID, repository ID and exact run head SHA
Independent verifier GETs server-side sha256 artifact digest and compares actual downloaded zip bytes with it, without trusting an inline claimed digest or upload action output
Verified archive contains only exact two named ordinary handover files, no path traversal, duplicates, extra files, zip bombs or symlinks; cold replay checks source against live GitHub GET
A coordinated alteration of BOTH context and event basis can still fool two-file offline-only self-consistency; verifier must demonstrably reject it against server anchored original file hashes
Altered archive bytes cannot match GitHub API stored digest; verifier must reject without running cold successor
Wrong artifact run id, source SHA, repository identity, missing digest, expired or missing artifact fail closed
Remote artifact lookup requires authenticated Actions read token; no ability to publish title, issue, PR, grant merge/Owner proof
Provider anchor is expiry-bound and repository administrator may delete it; no claim of signed owner custody or durable archive once expired
Read-only source replay still rejects changed input pin and grants no execution; provider artifact anchoring does not prove original Owner chat message
